# Topic 12 cover v01

Built-in image generation. New concept illustration, not research documents.

Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Topic 12 cover for a natural-history ecology atlas website, one new transparent PNG illustration.
Primary request: Create one detailed natural-history archive-and-nature vignette about gathering ecological knowledge from written records. Landscape 3:2 composition, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels.

Subject and arrangement: A small open field notebook with entirely blank, unruled cream leaf pages is the quiet central object. Several separate, entirely blank report papers are loosely fanned behind and beside the notebook, visibly individual sheets rather than one large rectangular block. A carefully rendered pressed leaf and a naturalist's botanical sprig rest across the blank pages and connect the papers to a small patch of reeds and living foliage along one edge. Include one small, realistic moth resting near the leaf as a discreet specimen detail; it must not dominate. Let the field plants and archive objects form one contiguous, cohesive arrangement with breathing room. Do not arrange them as separate floating icons.

Style and medium: Detailed watercolor and gouache natural-history atlas painting. Fine botanical edges, delicate leaf veins, convincing paper fibers and pigment texture within the objects, careful small anatomical details, soft natural light. Match the calm, finely observed forest-canopy and dried-herbarium cover aesthetic: muted olive and sage greens, warm cream, brown ink-like natural tones, gentle ochre accents. Painterly and tactile, not vector, cartoon, glossy 3D, product photography or a literal photorealistic book on a rectangle.

Framing and transparency: The whole vignette has an irregular organic silhouette. Leave clear transparent breathing room around it, with soft natural cutout edges and fine transparent gaps between leaves. Keep all important objects fully within the canvas. Use a genuine transparent alpha background with fully transparent corners. There is no backdrop, paper artboard, rectangular mat, frame, border or checkerboard. Any soft contact shading must be localized to the objects and must not become a rectangular ground.

Text: Absolutely no letters, numbers, words, handwriting, ruled writing lines, fake script or pseudotext anywhere. All notebook and report pages are completely unlettered and unruled. A botanical specimen may lie on them, but there are no document labels.

Avoid: Information dashboard, flowchart, arrows, connecting diagram lines, digital UI, screens, PDF logos, brands, seals, stamps, charts, map pins, grids, headers, labels, captions and watermarks. This is a conceptual natural-history illustration, not a depiction of actual research documents.
